_comment: Section 10 coaching. 3 escalating steps per scam type. The 'fact' line ALWAYS comes from here, never from the LLM. Step 3 is always the hang-up.

irs_gov.say: Can I have your name and badge number? I'll call the IRS back myself.
irs_gov.fact: The IRS usually contacts you by mail first, and never demands gift cards, crypto or wire transfers.

irs_gov.say: I'm not paying anything over the phone.
irs_gov.fact: You can check what you really owe at irs.gov/account.
Threats of arrest over unpaid taxes are a scam tactic.

immigration_uscis.say: I'll check this with my university's international office first.
immigration_uscis.fact: USCIS and ICE never ask for payment over the phone or in gift cards.

immigration_uscis.say: Please send me an official letter. I won't pay on this call.
immigration_uscis.fact: Check your case only at uscis.gov, or ask your international student office.
Deportation threats with a same-day 'fee' are a common scam against international students.

tech_support.say: I didn't ask for support. I'll contact the company myself.
tech_support.fact: Microsoft and Apple don't make unsolicited calls about viruses.

tech_support.say: I won't install anything or log in to my bank while you're on the line.
tech_support.fact: Remote-access apps let scammers see your screen and your accounts.
If you already gave access, disconnect from Wi-Fi and change your passwords.

rental_deposit.say: I'd like to see the place in person before paying anything.
rental_deposit.fact: Never pay a deposit for a place you haven't seen or a lease you haven't signed.

rental_deposit.say: Can you send me the property manager's official contact?
rental_deposit.fact: Requests for Zelle, wire or gift cards for a deposit are a red flag.

rental_deposit.say: I'm going to pass on this one, thanks.
rental_deposit.fact: Report fake listings to the site and to the campus scam map.

fake_job_check.say: I won't deposit a check and send money back.
fake_job_check.fact: Real employers never send a check and ask you to return part of it.

fake_job_check.say: Please email me the offer from a company address and I'll verify it.
fake_job_check.fact: Fake checks can bounce days later, and you owe the bank the money.
Check job offers with your career center before sending anything.

family_emergency.say: What's something only you and I would know?
family_emergency.fact: Scammers fake emergencies, and can clone a voice from short clips.

family_emergency.say: I'm going to call you back on your usual number.
family_emergency.fact: Bail, lawyers and hospitals don't take gift cards or crypto.
Call the person directly on a number you already know.

bank_impersonation.say: I'll call my bank back using the number on my card.
bank_impersonation.fact: Your bank will never ask for a one-time code, your PIN, or your password.

bank_impersonation.say: I won't share any codes or move my money.
bank_impersonation.fact: There is no such thing as a 'safe account'. That's where the scammer gets paid.

bank_impersonation.say: I'm hanging up and calling my bank directly.
bank_impersonation.fact: If you shared a code, call your bank's fraud line right away.

generic.say: Who exactly am I speaking with? I'll call you back on an official number.
generic.fact: Real organizations are fine with you calling them back.

generic.say: I don't make payments or share codes on calls I didn't make.
generic.fact: Pressure, secrecy and unusual payment methods are signs of a scam.
When in doubt, hang up and call back on a number you know.
